words.definition: the process by which a parent cell produces daughter cells
words.example: Cell division is required for growth, repair and reproduction.

words.definition: division of a cell nucleus and its chromosomes
words.example: Mitosis and meiosis are forms of nuclear division.

words.definition: nuclear division that produces genetically similar nuclei with the same chromosome number as the parent nucleus
words.example: Mitosis supports growth and tissue repair.

words.definition: a two-division process that produces haploid nuclei from a diploid cell and generates genetic variation
words.example: Meiosis produces gametes in many sexually reproducing organisms.

words.definition: an early division stage in which chromosomes condense and spindle organization begins
words.example: Chromosomes become visibly condensed during prophase.

words.definition: the division stage in which chromosomes or bivalents align at the cell equator
words.example: Chromosomes line up at the metaphase plate.

words.definition: the division stage in which chromosomes or chromatids separate and move toward opposite poles
words.example: Sister chromatids separate during anaphase of mitosis.

words.definition: the late division stage in which separated chromosome sets reach the poles and nuclei reform
words.example: Nuclear envelopes form around chromosome sets during telophase.

words.definition: division of the cytoplasm to form separate daughter cells
words.example: Cytokinesis follows nuclear division in many cells.

words.definition: a DNA molecule with associated proteins carrying genetic information
words.example: Each chromosome contains many genes.

words.definition: one of two identical DNA copies of a replicated chromosome joined at the centromere
words.example: Sister chromatids separate during mitotic anaphase.

words.definition: one of a pair of chromosomes with the same genes in corresponding loci, one inherited from each parent
words.example: Homologous chromosomes pair during meiosis I.

words.definition: having two sets of homologous chromosomes
words.example: Most human somatic cells are diploid.

words.definition: having one set of chromosomes
words.example: Human gametes are haploid.

words.definition: a cell division that reduces chromosome number from diploid to haploid
words.example: Meiosis I is a reduction division.

words.definition: failure of homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids to separate normally during cell division
words.example: Non-disjunction can produce gametes with abnormal chromosome numbers.

words.definition: a cell produced by division of a parent cell
words.example: Mitosis typically produces two daughter cells.

words.definition: a protein around which DNA is wrapped in eukaryotic chromosomes
words.example: DNA associates with histones to form chromatin.

words.definition: a hollow cytoskeletal filament made of tubulin that contributes to spindle formation and chromosome movement
words.example: Spindle microtubules attach to chromosomes during division.

words.definition: a pair of homologous chromosomes associated during meiosis I
words.example: Bivalents align at the equator during metaphase I.

words.definition: exchange of DNA between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes during meiosis
words.example: Crossing over creates new combinations of alleles.

words.definition: independent alignment of homologous chromosome pairs at the equator during meiosis I
words.example: Random orientation contributes to genetic variation among gametes.

words.definition: the process by which solvent molecules surround and interact with dissolved particles
words.example: Water molecules form hydration shells around dissolved ions during solvation.

words.definition: the amount of dissolved solute in a given quantity of solution
words.example: Increasing solute concentration can increase the tendency of water to move into a solution by osmosis.

words.definition: describing a solution with a higher effective solute concentration than a comparison solution or cell
words.example: An animal cell loses water in a hypertonic solution.

words.definition: describing a solution with a lower effective solute concentration than a comparison solution or cell
words.example: Water enters an animal cell placed in a hypotonic solution.

words.definition: describing two solutions with equal effective solute concentrations so there is no net osmotic water movement
words.example: Red blood cells maintain normal shape in an isotonic solution.

words.definition: the overall direction of water movement when movement in one direction exceeds movement in the other
words.example: Osmosis produces net water movement across a selectively permeable membrane.

words.definition: increase in cell volume caused by net water entry
words.example: An animal cell may undergo cell swelling in a hypotonic solution.

words.definition: rupture of a cell membrane and loss of cell integrity
words.example: Excessive water entry can cause cell lysis in an animal cell.

words.definition: shrinkage and wrinkling of an animal cell after water loss in a hypertonic solution
words.japanese: クレネーション・縮み
words.example: A red blood cell undergoes crenation in a strongly hypertonic solution.

words.definition: pressure exerted by the cell contents against the cell wall after water enters a plant cell
words.example: Turgor pressure helps support non-woody plant tissues.

words.definition: describing a plant cell swollen with water and pressing firmly against its cell wall
words.example: A well-watered plant cell is usually turgid.

words.definition: describing a plant cell with low turgor pressure
words.example: Plant cells become flaccid when they lose water.

words.definition: separation of the plasma membrane from the cell wall after substantial water loss from a plant cell
words.example: Plasmolysis occurs when plant tissue is placed in a strongly hypertonic solution.

words.definition: an organelle that collects and expels excess water from some freshwater protists
words.example: A contractile vacuole prevents excessive water accumulation in a freshwater protist.

words.definition: a solution with the same effective solute concentration as the cell or comparison solution
words.example: An isotonic solution causes no net volume change in many animal cells.

words.definition: net movement of water into or out of plant tissue across cell membranes due to differences in effective solute concentration
words.example: Changes in potato-cylinder mass can be used to investigate plant tissue osmosis.
